canonical_reconciliation.result: Q04F is already a canonical claim in both the pinned plan and assembly, and the claim crosswalk maps its staged review. It is not an uncanonicalized extra identifier; do not mint a duplicate or increase the 74/23 counts.

source_anchors.source: King Saud University, al-Qurtubi, Sūrah al-Kawthar
source_anchors.locator: electronic page label 602; verse 108:1, list of sixteen interpretations, eighth item
source_anchors.anchor: الثامن : أنه الإيثار ; قاله ابن كيسان
source_anchors.finding: This digital witness gives the interpretation as al-ithar and attributes it to Ibn Kaysan. The clause gives no oral isnad and does not identify Qurtubi as adopting this item as his preference.

source_anchors.source: Cairo Arabic Language Academy, al-Mu'jam al-Wasit
source_anchors.finding: The dictionary gives the verbal usage آثَرَه إيثارًا as choosing and preferring him, and separately records the idiom آثره على نفسه. This supports the lexical base, but does not by itself establish the intended object or ethical nuance of Qurtubi's bare noun phrase إنه الإيثار.

source_anchors.source: Current live Arabic and English Qurtubi rows
source_anchors.finding: Read-only inspection locates the exact Arabic claim at position 2383 in row 13239. English row 38030 has no checked Ibn Kaysan/al-ithar/altruism/preference wording.

It supports only the lexical base of choosing/preference; adding an object such as preferring another over oneself, or an ethical gloss such as altruism/selflessness, remains a contextual inference for scholarly review.

fidelity_reconciliation.voice: The source and staged review identify Ibn Kaysan as the named authority for the reported view; no transmission route or authentication is inferred.
fidelity_reconciliation.english_absence: Keep the corresponding English absence explicit. A parallel digital English witness does not replace row 38030 or prove its translator/edition.
fidelity_reconciliation.wording_attention: The pinned canonical plan and copied assembly describe the proposition as 'altruistic preference'. The newer lexical-scope checkpoint cautions that 'altruistic' and supplying an unstated object add context not directly present in the bare Arabic phrase. This is a review flag, not an approved correction.
fidelity_reconciliation.decision: Do not edit the canonical plan or assembly, change live English, or promote this wording to publication-ready state in this run. Ask an independent Arabic/English reviewer whether the current proposition exceeds the source and what minimal neutral gloss, if any, is warranted.

review.required: Independent scholar to reconcile the lexical-scope note with the canonical statement and assess whether the ethical/object nuance is justified by the source. Preserve the English absence and named-reporter boundary.
